title: Made a trailer for my game, can you tell what it is about?
author: SwahReddit
selftext:
I'm trying to figure out if the trailer works on its own. After watching, could you tell me:

\- what do you think you actually do in this game?

\- what genre is it?

\- what's the goal, and why would you want to make more potions?



More info:

\>!Basically Infinite Craft but with gameplay and a goal. You build a factory, but instead of every recipe being prebuilt, you create your own to answer whatever the town needs.!<

\>!https://potionfactory.swahstudio.com/!<



Some stuff I'm specifically unsure about:

\- does it look like a factory/automation game or more like a crafting puzzle game? I've had someone read it as a puzzle game before

\- does "brew anything" feel believable, or does it look like a fixed recipe list?

An LLM decides what word combos turn into at runtime. The trailer itself isn't gameplay capture, it's animated in code (Remotion) to show where the game is heading. I can also go into how I made the trailer in the comments if anyone is interested.

comments.author: Vangrid5857
comments.body: The trailer looks really interesting! My understanding is that you combine cards to create new resources, then use them to fight viruses and zombies and protect the village. I couldn’t tell from the trailer whether certain combinations have special effects or are more effective against specific enemies. From a game design perspective, that could be a fun direction: letting players experiment to discover the best solution for each monster. Is that part of the gameplay?

replies.author: SwahReddit
replies.body:
Thanks, that's pretty much it! You combine words to invent potions, then automate making them to protect the town.

Right now there aren't per-enemy matchups. Two things matter:

\- Traits: each potion recipe needs words with certain traits (small, terrestrial, gas, etc.). You combine words until you find ones with the right traits, then grow your factory around these transformations.

\- Potency: every transformation a potion goes through makes it stronger, so longer chains give more progress per potion.

replies.author: Vangrid5857
replies.body:
Are recipe exploration and factory automation meant to happen at the same time?   
If so, have you considered structuring them as a relay: players explore to discover recipes, then plan and automate production?   
You could also introduce town crises in stages, giving players time to experiment and build their production lines before seeing them put to use.   
I wonder if that would help the two parts feel connected without interrupting each other. Personally, I think I’d struggle to keep up if I had to manage both at once!

replies.author: SwahReddit
replies.body:
Yes recipe exploration / factory automation are done in the same gameplay space. I'm currently trying to balance the time between recipe exploration and factory automation, I'll focus on that in the next playtests. What I've got right now sounds similar to what you suggested: there's an architect card that will take as input the card you crafted, and will lay off ghost shapes of all factory pieces you'll need. Then you craft them using another mechanic. 

You're also right for the town crisis stages - it's exactly how it works in the game, 3 stages per town. They constantly generate zombies / fire / viruses to keep some adversity in the game. 

Thanks for the thoughts on this, happy to see that you've understood the base gameplay from that video!
